subject: LedgerLink — Post-call spend scenarios & batching/caching playbook
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Stanton <olivia@ledgerlink.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: LedgerLink post-call — cost scenarios, key pain, and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we aligned on the top items and where we go next.

What we heard (pain & goals):
- High token spend on user-facing summarization flows (chat and email triage) — current monthly token volume ~280M tokens.
- Tight budget ceiling for Q3; procurement wants a predictable TCO and a clear pilot ROI before a commitment.
- Latency SLOs: 200–300ms P95 on top-tier chat; some endpoints can tolerate 500ms.
- Security: must run in VPC with KMS-managed keys for any pilot data.

Cost/TCO levers we discussed (high level):
- Batching: expected 20–40% per-token cost reduction for the summarization pipeline if we implement 50–80% request coalescing during peak windows.
- KV/prefix caching: up to 15% savings for repeat context patterns (user profile + system prompt).
- Model selection / quantization: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant for lower-criticality routing could yield 25–35% CPU/GPU cost reduction with small quality tradeoffs.
- Dedicated vs hosted routing: Dedicated pools give predictable throughput but require a 3-month minimum reserve (savings depend on utilization).

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed timeline):
1) We’ll send a short pilot SOW + two cost scenarios (conservative / aggressive) by Monday (attached).
2) You to share: expected monthly active users for the summarization flow and any redlines from security (VPC/KMS) so we can finalize pilot footprint.
3) If procurement wants an internal TCO slide, Marissa will prepare a 1-pager comparing hosted vs dedicated for the pilot.

Attachment: ledgerlink-pilot-cost-model.xlsx (pilot token assumptions, batching uplift scenarios)

Thanks — Mark

--
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Olivia Stanton <olivia@ledgerlink.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ledgerlink.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 15:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: LedgerLink post-call — cost scenarios, key pain, and next steps

Thanks Markus — useful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 280M token estimate is for the entire org; the pilot scope should focus on the customer support summarization flow (~45M tokens/month expected in pilot).
- Procurement flagged the need for an explicit data retention policy in the SOW (30 days for pilot logs, none for customer content).
- Can you include an example throughput profile (QPS and burst) for the two cost scenarios? That helps our infra team size the dedicated pool if we go that route.

I’ll loop in procurement to review the SOW once you send it. Also happy to take a quick 20-min handoff call with your ops lead next week.

Olivia
Director of Product, LedgerLink
olivia@ledgerlink.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Stanton <olivia@ledgerlink.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: LedgerLink post-call — cost scenarios, key pain, and next steps

Hi Olivia — attaching the draft SOW and the cost workbook the team mentioned. Highlights pulled from the workbook before you open it: 

- Pilot baseline (45M tokens/month): Hosted conservative path: $6,300/month; Hosted aggressive (with 35% batching + 10% cache hit): $4,400/month.
- Dedicated pilot estimate (reserved small pool with burst to hosted): ~$3,900/month equivalent if utilization >= 70%. Break-even at ~65% utilization over the 3-month commit.
- Latency tradeoffs: with batching enabled we target P95 ~250–320ms; with dedicated low-latency path (no batching) P95 ~180–220ms depending on model choice.

Quick notes on assumptions used in the workbook: average tokens per request 420, average requests/day 35k during pilot, batching uplift assumes 50% effective coalescing during peak 2 hours/day. See sheet 'Assumptions' for full details.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Olivia / procurement: confirm pilot scope (45M vs other) and the retention requirement — then we finalize SOW.
- Lauren: ops/infra to do a short sizing for Dedicated pool and confirm burst mechanics.
- Markus / Marissa: once SOW is approved, we prepare a one-slide ROI with 12-week projection to help procurement.

Attachments: ledgerlink-pilot-sow-draft.docx, ledgerlink-pilot-cost-model.xlsx

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Olivia Stanton <olivia@ledgerlink.com>

Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 18:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: LedgerLink post-call — cost scenarios, key pain, and next steps

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear scenarios. Procurement and I reviewed the workbook and have two quick asks before we proceed: 

1) Please add a short appendix that lists the security controls and the KMS flow for pilot keys (who has key access, rotation cadence).
2) Can you show a sensitivity table that maps batching effectiveness (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%) to monthly cost so procurement can see downside/upside?

If you can get a revised SOW + workbook with those two items by Monday EOD, we’ll aim to route approval internally the following week. If that timeline is tight, let us know and we’ll prioritize a narrower scope.

Also happy to set the 20-min ops call next Tue 10:00am PT if that works for your infra lead.

Olivia
